findings.evidence: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/Holder.lean:53 `theorem memLp_of_bilin (hf : MemLp f p μ) (hg : MemLp g q μ) : MemLp (fun x ↦ B (f x) (g x)) r μ`; Mathlib/Analysis/ENNReal/Holder.lean:65 `instance instInfty (p) : HolderTriple p ∞ p`; Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Monotonicity.lean:218 `MemLp.of_nnnorm_le_mul`.
findings.fix: Delete `MemLp.clm_comp_of_ae_nnnorm_le` and prove the `MemLp` step in `clm_comp_of_continuousOn` as `(ContinuousLinearMap.compL 𝕜 E F G).memLp_of_bilin p (memLp_top_of_bound hA C hC) hB`, or with `hB.of_nnnorm_le_mul hA' hC'` using `opNNNorm_comp_le`. The Hölder triple `(∞, p, p)` comes from `ENNReal.HolderTriple.instInfty` and `.symm`.
findings.issue: `MemLp.clm_comp_of_ae_nnnorm_le` is a wrapper: it is `ContinuousLinearMap.memLp_of_bilin` applied to `compL` with an `L^∞` left factor. `MemLp.clm_comp_of_continuousOn` (line 55) inherits the duplication, and `eLpNorm_clm_comp_le_of_ae_nnnorm_le` (line 36) only adds a pointwise bound on top of `eLpNorm_le_nnreal_smul_eLpNorm_of_ae_le_mul`.

findings.evidence: Both lemmas use the same proof: `Metric.uniformContinuous(On)_iff` → `filter_upwards [hρ.eventually (gt_mem_nhds _)]` → `dist_comm` → `(ρ i).dist_normed_convolution_le ... |>.trans_lt (half_lt_self hε)` (Convolution.lean:167-173 vs 185-192).
findings.fix: Keep the `On` version and reprove the global one from it: `tendstoUniformlyOn_univ.1 (tendstoUniformlyOn_normed_convolution hρ one_pos (hg.uniformContinuousOn) hg.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable)`. Alternatively, put the global lemma first and derive the `On` version from the shared core.
findings.issue: `tendstoUniformlyOn_normed_convolution` repeats the epsilon/delta argument of `tendstoUniformly_normed_convolution` (line 163) line for line, so the same estimate is proved twice.

summary: The chain-rule, pair and graph-composition results are new, but the `L^∞ × Lᵖ` composition `MemLp` lemma wraps Mathlib's Hölder bilinear API, and the new `tendstoUniformlyOn_normed_convolution` clones the proof of its global sibling in the same file.
